facts.text: I have pain in my belly.
I have pain in my back.
The pain came on suddenly during the night.
I haven't had any other stomach or bowel upset.
I finished a 10-day course of clindamycin yesterday.
I had cellulitis in my left calf.
I've had deep vein thromboses (blood clots) several times.
I take medication for my diabetes.

findings.name: abdominal examination
findings.result: Mild to moderate epigastric tenderness; normal bowel sounds.

findings.name: skin examination of the legs
findings.result: Mild resolving cellulitis of the right calf.

findings.name: complete blood count
findings.result: Hemoglobin 10.3 g/dL; white blood cell count 12.9×10^9/L; platelets 303×10^9/L.

findings.name: urea and electrolytes
findings.result: Urea 8.7 mmol/L; creatinine 111 μmol/L; sodium 144 mmol/L; potassium 4.1 mmol/L; calcium 2.02 mmol/L.

findings.name: chest radiograph
findings.result: Slight fluid overload, cardiomegaly, and interstitial shadowing.

findings.name: CT of the chest, abdomen and pelvis
findings.result: Subtle, non-specific bilateral adrenal enhancing lesions.

findings.name: short synacthen test
findings.result: No appreciable rise in cortisol: baseline 95 nmol/L; 60 min 113 nmol/L; 90 min 132 nmol/L.

gold.reasoning: 1. Gastro-oesophageal reflux disease was initially considered because of epigastric pain — “The initial impression was possible gastro-oesophageal reflux disease.” 2. Sepsis was considered given elevated inflammatory markers and co-morbidities — “…it was important to rule out sepsis or malignancy.” 3. Malignancy was considered due to age, presentation, and risk factors — “…it was important to rule out sepsis or malignancy.” 4. Adrenal metastases were considered based on CT findings of bilateral adrenal lesions — “the differential diagnosis for which included metastases, infection, granulomatous disease or haemorrhage.” 5. Adrenal infection was considered on imaging grounds — “the differential diagnosis for which included metastases, infection, granulomatous disease or haemorrhage.” 6. Granulomatous adrenal disease was considered among imaging differentials — “the differential diagnosis for which included metastases, infection, granulomatous disease or haemorrhage.”

quotes.f003: acute onset abdominal and back pain that began during the night
quotes.f006: One day earlier he had completed a 10-day course of clindamycin

f005: 'Gastrointestinal disturbance' is vague; written as a blanket denial of other gastrointestinal symptoms, which answers only the open question.
f007: The history says left calf (s002); the examination says right calf (s005). The fact keeps the history's side.
f015: Only implied by the hospital course ('withholding diabetic medications', s011); the drug names are not given.

leakage.reason: Radiology report names bilateral adrenal lesions (the organ of the gold), not the haemorrhage; a written report keeps its conclusion.

source_issues: Cellulitis side: left calf in the history (s002), right calf on examination (s005).
s011 says he 'remained hypotensive', but the presentation blood pressure was 200/132 mmHg (s004).
The ECG shows a paced rhythm, but no pacemaker is mentioned in the history.
notes: Index visit: the emergency presentation with acute abdominal and back pain that began during the night (s001-s007); the CT and the short synacthen test (s010, s012) are later findings of the same admission and carry time 'after admission'.

s011 is cited only for the fact that he takes diabetes medication; the rest of s011 (INR normalising after vitamin K, persistent hypotension, ongoing pain with new nausea, lethargy and abdominal distension, normal glucose after diabetic medications were withheld) is hospital course after treatment and is not part of the case.
No pacemaker fact is written: the source only reports a paced rhythm on the ECG.
Calcium is grouped with urea and electrolytes because it was reported with the same admission chemistry.

excluded_sentences.reason: Clinician's initial impression (possible gastro-oesophageal reflux disease); interpretation, not a finding.
Treatment (warfarin withheld, vitamin K, intravenous fluids); not part of the case.
